label: NO. 001 · FOUNDING EDITION
note: A career-intelligence newspaper for a senior staff product designer. This first edition establishes the baseline; it is not a claim that every item broke today.
headline: The title may stay. The job is moving.
summary: For a senior staff product designer, the useful question is not whether AI will rename the role. It is which decisions, skills and responsibilities employers increasingly expect you to own.
body: My take: don’t rush to replace your title with an AI label. Build a stronger story about the scope you own: identifying the right problem, shaping behavior across a system, testing it with people, and bringing teams to a defensible decision.

The evidence is directional, not a prediction about your employer. Figma’s June 2026 survey reports more overlap between design and development. Its sample reflects product builders, not the whole labor market. Separately, OpenAI is recruiting a Product Designer for consumer experiences whose responsibilities include agent interactions, trust and user control. The familiar title remains; the work described is changing.

For your next portfolio revision, my recommendation is one case study showing an AI-enabled workflow from ambiguity to a working prototype, including evaluation, failure recovery and the choices you rejected. Show the judgment behind what ships, not merely how quickly you produced screens.

This newspaper will separate three things: what changed, what it could mean for your career, and one worthwhile action. Jobs will be evaluated for actual scope and fit—not recommended just because an AI company posted them.
priorities: Track role scope before title inflation: ownership, influence and outcomes matter more than a fashionable label.
Review the exploratory consumer-design opening below if San Francisco and hands-on IC work appeal.
Pick one portfolio case where you can demonstrate judgment about AI behavior, not just AI-assisted production.

stories.title: The boundary between design and development is getting thinner.
stories.summary: Figma’s 2026 report says 41% of designers in its survey participate in development, while 60% of developers do design work. These are survey findings from a design-tool vendor, not a forecast that senior design roles disappear.
stories.takeaway: Bart’s take: strengthen your ability to prototype and critique working systems, while keeping research, product framing and design quality central.

stories.title: Faster prototypes are not the same as better product decisions.
stories.summary: A preprint describes an experiment with 50 designers and 50 product managers. Among task completers, access to Figma Make was associated with roughly 20% shorter completion times, with larger gains for PMs. Standardized tasks and completion-time results do not establish whole-job replacement.
stories.takeaway: Bart’s take: test where AI saves you time on real work, and measure quality and rework alongside speed.

stories.title: OpenAI: Product Designer, Consumer Verticals
stories.summary: San Francisco HQ; advertised base pay $245K–$310K plus equity. The posting seeks substantial consumer-product experience, zero-to-one work and strong interaction craft. It includes designing agentic experiences and user control. The title does not establish a Senior Staff-equivalent level.
stories.takeaway: Investigate, not yet an apply recommendation. Potential fit if your portfolio shows complex consumer systems; location, compensation goals and level equivalence still need checking.

coverage: Sources checked October 15, 2026. Older research is labeled as background, not today’s news. A job checked today is not necessarily newly posted today.
